statements.t: During 2024, we recorded a reach-forward loss of $1,770 million on the T-7A Red Hawk program that was primarily driven by projected increases in supplier cost estimates.
We expect this disruption to continue into 2027 and result in abnormal production costs, which are expensed as incurred.

If we are unable to successfully negotiate successor agreements with our unions that our employees will ratify, we may experience additional work stoppages in the future and/or higher than anticipated costs, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

Our total backlog represents the estimated transaction prices on unsatisfied and partially satisfied performance obligations to our customers where we believe it is probable that we will collect the consideration due and where no contingencies remain before we and the customer are required to perform.
We continue to work toward stabilizing production at 47 per month and now expect to stabilize in 2027.
Consistent with our focus on safety and quality, after demonstrating stability at rate 47 for a period of time, we plan to increase to rate 52.
If we are unable to deliver aircraft and/or increase production rates consistent with our assumptions, our financial position, results of operations and cash flows will be further adversely affected.
statements.was: If we are unable to deliver aircraft and/or increase production rates or certify the 737-7 and 737-10 models consistent with our assumptions, our financial position, results of operations and cash flows will be adversely affected.

statements.t: We are targeting a production rate of approximately three aircraft per month.
We expect to complete production of the 767 commercial program by 2027.
The 777 accounting quantity reflects the number of units we expect to produce and deliver by 2029.
We expect operations to continue to be disrupted through the first half of 2027.
On the 777X program, we continue to work through certification flight testing and expect to receive approval on the final phases of flight testing by the end of 2026.
We continue to expect first delivery of the 777-9 to occur in 2027.
We continue to anticipate first delivery of the 777-8 Freighter to occur approximately two years after the first delivery of the 777-9.
We are continuing to follow the lead of the FAA as we work through the certification process and the ultimate timing will be determined by the regulators.
During the third quarter of 2026, we decided to delay planned production rate increases with the next increase beyond eight per month now planned to begin in December 2026.
Subsequent increases in production rates will be enabled by the completion of expansion projects underway in our Charleston facility and the ability of our supply chain to support higher rates.
We continue to expect capital expenditures in 2026 to be higher than in 2025.
We anticipate that these credit lines will primarily serve as back-up liquidity to support our general corporate borrowing needs.
At S&P, we are rated BBB- with a stable outlook, and at Moody’s, we are rated Baa3 with a stable outlook.

We expect to be able to access capital markets when we require additional funding to support our operations, pay off existing debt, address impacts to our business related to market developments, fund outstanding financing commitments or meet other business requirements; however, a number of factors could increase the cost of borrowing, jeopardize our ability to incur debt on terms acceptable to us, and…

These factors include downgrades in our credit ratings, disruptions or declines in the global capital markets, a decline in our financial performance or outlook, a delay in our ability to ramp up production and deliveries, and changes in demand for our products and services.
